issues.title: Division by zero crashes the program
issues.body:
When I enter `10/0`, the program crashes with an unhandled exception instead of showing an error message.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Run the calculator
2. Type `10/0`
3. Program crashes with ZeroDivisionError traceback

**Expected behavior:** Show a user-friendly error message like "Error: Division by zero" and re-prompt.

issues.title: Empty input crashes the program
issues.body:
Pressing Enter without typing anything crashes the program with an IndexError.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Run the calculator
2. Press Enter without typing anything
3. Program crashes

**Expected behavior:** Show an error message or re-prompt the user.

issues.title: Division returns integer instead of decimal — 7/2 gives 3
issues.body:
The division operation truncates decimal results. `7/2` returns `3` instead of `3.5`. `10/3` returns `3` instead of `3.333...`.

It seems to be using integer division (`//`) instead of true division (`/`).

issues.title: Whitespace in expressions causes parse error
issues.body:
Entering `2 + 3` (with spaces around the operator) causes a parse error. Only `2+3` (no spaces) works.

Users naturally type spaces around operators, so this should be handled.

issues.title: Operator precedence is wrong — 2+3*4 returns 20 instead of 14
issues.body:
The calculator does not respect standard math operator precedence. Multiplication and division should be evaluated before addition and subtraction.

**Example:**
- `2+3*4` should return `14` but returns `20`
- `10-2*3` should return `4` but returns `24`

It seems to evaluate strictly left to right. Fixing this requires reworking the expression parser to handle precedence correctly.

issues.title: Add support for parentheses in expressions
issues.body:
The calculator should support parentheses to let users control evaluation order.

**Examples:**
- `(2+3)*4` should return `20`
- `10/(2+3)` should return `2`

This would require updating the expression parser to handle nested groupings and recursive evaluation.

issues.title: Add history feature
issues.body: It would be nice to have some kind of history feature. Maybe like pressing the up arrow or something?

issues.title: It crashed yesterday
issues.body: I was doing some sums yesterday and it just crashed on me. Lost what I was working on. Please fix this, it's really frustrating.

issues.title: Calculator gives wrong answer for large numbers
issues.body: When I put in really big numbers the answer comes out wrong. Smaller numbers seem fine.

issues.title: Doesn't work on my machine
issues.body: I followed the README but nothing happens when I run it. I'm on Windows 11. Is this supposed to work on Windows?

issues.title: Dividing odd numbers gives the wrong answer
issues.body: If I divide an odd number by 2 the result is off. `7/2` shows `3` and `9/2` shows `4`. I'd expect `3.5` and `4.5`.

issues.title: Can't use spaces when typing a calculation
issues.body: Typing `4 * 5` gives `Invalid input`. Typing `4*5` works. It took me a while to work out that the spaces were the problem.

issues.title: Support brackets like (1+2)*3
issues.body: Would love to be able to group parts of a calculation with brackets, e.g. `(1+2)*3` = `9`.

issues.title: Pressing Ctrl-D at the prompt prints a traceback
issues.body:
Pressing Ctrl-D (end of input) at the `>` prompt dumps a Python traceback ending in `EOFError: EOF when reading a line` instead of exiting cleanly. Ctrl-C does the same with `KeyboardInterrupt`.

**Expected:** print `Goodbye!` and exit, the same as typing `quit`.

issues.title: Typing QUIT in capitals doesn't exit
issues.body: `quit` and `exit` work, but `QUIT` or `Exit` print `Invalid input` and keep the calculator running. The exit commands should be case-insensitive.

issues.title: Negative numbers give Invalid input
issues.body: `-5+3` gives `Invalid input` instead of `-2`. Same for `3*-2`. There's no way to enter a negative number.

issues.title: Decimal numbers aren't accepted
issues.body: `3.5+1` gives `Invalid input`. Only whole numbers seem to work. It'd be useful to calculate with prices and measurements.

issues.title: Remove the global result variable from calculator.py
issues.body: `add()`, `subtract()`, `multiply()` and `divide()` all write their answer to a module-level `result` global before returning it. Nothing reads it. It makes the functions impure and harder to test. They should just return the value. `test_evaluate_leaves_no_module_state` covers it.

issues.title: Remove unused parse_expression()
issues.body: `parse_expression()` in `calculator.py` isn't called anywhere. `evaluate()` does its own tokenising. The only reference is an import in `tests/test_calculator.py`. Delete it along with the import.

issues.title: Add type hints and docstrings to calculator.py
issues.body: None of the functions in `calculator.py` or `main.py` have type hints or docstrings. Adding them would make the code easier to pick up. No behaviour changes.

issues.title: Add an exponent operator
issues.body: It would be handy to raise numbers to a power, e.g. `2^3` = `8` (or `2**3`, like Python).

issues.title: Use Python's eval() to fix the parsing bugs
issues.body: The hand-written parser in `evaluate()` is behind most of the open bugs: precedence, spaces, negative numbers, parentheses. Python can already do all of this. Replacing the body of `evaluate()` with `return eval(expr)` is a one-line change that fixes them all at once, and the existing tests should pass.

issues.title: Require Python 3.12
issues.body: `pyproject.toml` says `requires-python = ">=3.9"`, but 3.9 is end-of-life. Bump it to `>=3.12` so we can use newer syntax. It's a one-line change.
